title: Gideon and the Salt
premise: Quentin Whitlock poisons herself slowly for a living, tasting the king's food while secretly keeping ledgers for a guild that smuggles memories, names, and other impossible cargo out of a country that was officially dissolved twenty years ago. When a dying courier presses a salt-stained map into her hands, Quentin learns she is the last living heir to the door out of Old Vessany — a border that exists only in inherited memory — and that the Crown's inquisitors will burn anyone who remembers it. Hunted by the taster-master who raised her and shadowed by a guildsman who may be her father's killer, she must gather three keys of remembrance before the last salt-tide closes the door forever. In the end Quentin chooses not escape but testimony: she holds the door open long enough for the country's exiled dead to be remembered back into existence, paying with her own name, which is struck from every ledger including her own.
about_author: Petra Villalobos is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing the paperwork of defunct nations. She writes about borders, hunger, and the people who keep records no one asked them to keep.

chapters.title: The Taster's Portion
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. A night at court: Quentin tastes seven dishes, feels the familiar numbness spread, then slips belowstairs to update the guild's ledgers. We learn her double life and her rule: never read what you record. Emotional beat: controlled loneliness, the comfort of routine.

chapters.title: Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. She catalogs the week's cargo — a stolen lullaby, a widow's legal name, a jar of sea-salt from a drowned province — and realizes one entry was written in her late mother's hand. Emotional beat: unease; the past reaching through paperwork.

chapters.title: The Courier at the Fish Gate
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. A bleeding stranger finds her at dawn, presses a salt-crusted map into her hands, and dies saying 'the door knows your blood.' Inquisitors arrive; Quentin hides the map inside her tasting ledger. Emotional beat: terror fused with reluctant inheritance.

chapters.title: What the King Eats
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Her taster-master, Serle, notices her shaking hands and offers a promotion — permanent immunity work, which means never leaving the palace again. Quentin understands it as a cage dressed as honor. Emotional beat: claustrophobic kindness.

chapters.title: Salt on the Tongue
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Following the map's first clue, she tastes a grain of the map itself and experiences a flash-memory of a coastline that appears on no chart. The guild's fence, Marrow, confirms: this is an heir-map, and heirs are hunted. Emotional beat: vertigo of belonging to something erased.

chapters.title: The Guild of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. She seeks the guild's hidden chapter-house and instead finds it emptied, its members arrested overnight. One survivor, a boy called Finch, gives her a key of remembrance disguised as a debt-token. Emotional beat: guilt — her ledger entries were used as evidence.

chapters.title: Serle's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Serle. The taster-master reports to the inquisitors, revealing he has tracked Quentin since childhood and believes protecting her requires surrendering the map. His tenderness makes him more dangerous. Emotional beat: love distorted into control.

chapters.title: A Country That No Longer Exists
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. On the road with Finch, she crosses terrain where signs of Old Vessany flicker only when she speaks its name aloud. They shelter with a woman who remembers being a citizen of nowhere. Emotional beat: grief as geography.

chapters.title: The Second Key
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. In a flooded chapel they retrieve the second key — a bell that rings only for those the law forgot. Quentin must give up a true memory of her mother to lift it. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: The Man Who Sold the Door
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. A guildsman named Corvane intercepts them, claiming Quentin's father betrayed the guild and sold the door's location before dying. He offers passage in exchange for the map. Emotional beat: doubt poisoning inheritance.

chapters.title: Immunity
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Captured by inquisitors, Quentin survives interrogation because decades of poison have made her body refuse truth-serum too. She escapes during her own 'confession,' leaving Serle wounded and weeping. Emotional beat: her curse revealed as armor.

chapters.title: Finch's Debt
chapters.summary: POV Finch. The boy reveals he was paid to lead her to Corvane, but has decided she is worth more than the payment. They burn his debt-token together. Emotional beat: chosen loyalty over purchased service.

chapters.title: The Salt-Tide Calendar
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Marrow's surviving notes show the door opens only at the great salt-tide — eleven days away — and only once all three keys are joined. The third key lies inside the palace, in the royal vault of confiscated things. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Return to the Table
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Quentin walks back into the palace voluntarily, resuming her post as cover. At the king's table she recognizes the dish: seasoned with salt from Old Vessany. Someone above is already eating the country. Emotional beat: cold fury.

chapters.title: The Vault of Confiscated Things
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. With Finch as lookout, she descends into the vault and finds shelves of seized memory-objects — and the third key, a door-knocker from her family's house. Serle catches her there and does not raise the alarm. Emotional beat: mercy arriving from the wrong direction.

chapters.title: What Serle Swallowed
chapters.summary: POV Serle. He confesses he tested poisons on Quentin deliberately, building her immunity as an experiment ordered after her parents' arrest — and that her father died refusing to sell the door. Serle lets her go, taking her place in the vault. Emotional beat: inheritance reframed; sacrifice as apology.

chapters.title: Corvane's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Corvane corners them at the coast, reveals he killed her father on the Crown's contract, and demands the keys as ransom for Finch's life. Quentin trades the map — now useless without the keys — and buys Finch free. Emotional beat: ruthless arithmetic of love.

chapters.title: The Last Salt-Tide
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. At the drowned harbor, the tide begins. The three keys fuse into a threshold only her blood can open. Behind her, inquisitors; ahead, a doorway standing in seawater, humming with everyone Old Vessany lost. Emotional beat: awe edged with terror.

chapters.title: The Door Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Crossing the threshold, she meets the accumulated dead of the erased country, including her mother's recorded voice in the door's memory. She learns the truth: the door doesn't lead out — it leads back, into witness. Emotional beat: revelation dissolving the plan to flee.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Climax. Instead of escaping alone, Quentin turns the door outward and reads aloud from her own ledgers, restoring the names of the vanished into living memory while the inquisitors close in. Each name spoken strengthens the country's ghost-shape; each costs her a memory of her own. Emotional beat: defiant, costly justice outside the law.

chapters.title: The Unwritten Name
chapters.summary: POV Finch. The tide closes. Quentin remains on the threshold, alive but unnamed — struck from guild rolls, court records, even Finch's memory of her face. He carries her blank ledger out of the surf. Emotional beat: mourning someone still breathing.

chapters.title: A Taste of Salt
chapters.summary: POV Finch (with Quentin present, unnamed). Months later, Finch runs the rebuilt guild under new rules: nothing impossible gets traded, everything remembered gets kept. An unnamed woman comes to taste his cooking and smiles at the salt. Emotional beat: quiet continuation — inheritance passed on, survival redefined as remembrance.
